title: Establish canonical token-census and quota-reconciliation protocol for paused/resumed streaming sessions
creator: Aisha Carter
description:
Problem: Customers report inconsistent billing when WebSocket/Stream sessions are paused, resumed, or when clients reconnect after flaky networks. Root causes observed include: duplicated fragment replay, tokenizer drift between client and server, different finalization heuristics for incomplete sessions, and interactions between rate-limiter callbacks and provisional crediting logic.

Goal: Define and implement a canonical token-census protocol and quota-reconciliation flow that guarantees: deterministic final token attribution for interrupted streams, idempotent resume behavior across reconnects, bounded provisional credits during pauses, and clear invariants to allow downstream billing and quota systems to charge exactly once.

Out of scope: full redesign of rate-limiter; replacing streaming transport (ws vs http2). This ticket focuses on protocol semantics, enforcement points, and server-side reconciliation logic.
acceptance_criteria: Specification doc describing token-census checkpoints and their wire-format (session-checkpoint-id, cumulative-user-tokens, cumulative-system-tokens, checkpoint-hmac)
Server implements checkpoint anchoring in stream coordinator: checkpoints are created at stable message boundaries and persisted to durable store before acknowledging terminal fragments
Resume semantics: client-supplied checkpoint ID must be validated; server must refuse speculative replay beyond last committed checkpoint and transparently reconcile any provisional credits
Billing pipeline produces identical final token tallies for test harness scenarios: graceful pause, abrupt disconnect, multi-reconnect resume, and mid-session model switch
Unit and e2e tests (simulated flaky networks) demonstrate no double-charging and correct quota decrements under P95 latency and high-concurrency conditions
Observability: new dashboards populate with checkpoint-create/commit rates, provisional-credit amounts, and reconciliation-failure alerts
implementation_notes: Add lightweight checkpoint record to session metadata (small monotonic checkpoint counter + cumulative token counts). Persist to existing session store (Redis with write-through to Postgres for >1 hour sessions).

Change stream coordinator: create 'commit' barrier before marking session as terminal; commit barrier flushes KV-cache delta and writes checkpoint with HMAC (session secret) to prevent client spoofing.

Modify provisional-crediting path: provisional credits are issued but associated with the latest committed checkpoint ID. If session restarts at earlier checkpoint, provisional credits are rolled back atomically during reconciliation.

Token counting: canonicalize on the server-side tokenizer for all supported model families; on resume, if client-provided token deltas do not match server canonicalization, flag as 'tokenization-drift' and start conservative reconciliation (choose server counts), record incident for fraud detection.

Rate-limiter interaction: suspend quota enforcement for a short grace window when a valid resume checkpoint is received to avoid mid-reconnect double-debits; implement compensating transactions if resume fails after grace window.
Backward compatibility shim: for older clients without checkpoint capability, fall back to heuristics with increased provisional-credit caps and a slower reconciliation path to avoid disruption.
test_plan: Unit tests: checkpoint encode/decode, HMAC validation failures, provisional-credit rollbacks
Integration tests: simulated pause/resume flows over WS and SSE with randomized fragment reorderings
Chaos tests: inject disconnects and duplicate frames at various points to validate idempotency and no double-billing across 10k simulated sessions
Billing smoke test: run end-to-end billing pipeline against synthetic sessions and assert canonical final tallies match expected ground truth
Benchmark: measure commit latency added by checkpoint write under 99th percentile concurrent sessions; must keep additional latency < 12ms on median commit path
rollout_plan: Feature flag behind 'checkpointed_streaming' controlled per-customer; start with internal customers and non-production orgs
Canary group: 5% hosted traffic and all Dedicated test clusters; monitor reconciliation-failure rate and billing delta metrics
Escalation playbook: automatic rollback on >0.5% reconciliation failures over 10m or any customer-visible billing regressions
Gradual ramp to 100% over 3 weeks with weekly audits of reconciled vs provisional credits
